title: ImageNet networks judge by texture, not shape
body: Humans recognise objects by shape; ImageNet-trained CNNs lean heavily on texture, so a cat with elephant skin texture becomes an elephant to the model. Geirhos's 2019 stylised experiments exposed the bias. It explains some adversarial fragility and motivated shape-bias training. The machines mastered our benchmark without seeing as we see, a distinction deployment keeps rediscovering.
source_hint: Geirhos et al., ICLR 2019, texture bias
